text.p: - Eleven bullets killed an American competitor, the newspaper writes referring to the street murder of a prominent U.S. businessman who was fighting a legal battle for control of the five-star Radisson-Slavjanskaya hotel in Moscow.

- Deputy Security Council secretary Boris Berezovsky's double citizenship, if confirmed, would be incompatible with his state post, writes the daily in connection with its report last week about Berezovsky being a citizen of Israel as well as Russia.
- A seperate department in the presidential administration has been set up to run the affairs of the "power ministers". The head of the new control structure has not been yet named.
- President Bill Clinton is dreaming about a deserved victory and his rival Bob Dole has to think about a deserved defeat.
- The deputies of Russia's parliament have agreed to freeze export taxes for oil and gas.
- President Boris Yeltsin's former bodyguard Alexander Korzhakov has brought to court a case against the head of state and his administration to "protect his honor and dignity".
- A group of Russian scientists is offering a solution to end all the concerns of the West about the future of the Chernobyl nuclear plant in Ukraine.
- Bill Clinton's victory is practically predetermined.
- Russia's trade unions expect 10 million people to take part in today's protest action against the government's economic policy.
- Unemployent has grown by 1.5 times in Moscow over the last twelve months.
